notable_absence.finding: The page states 'A root account is required to run this command and collect all the server information' - an OS-level privilege requirement - but never mentions any Couchbase RBAC role, even though the tool's output can include sensitive data (hence the --log-redaction-level and --bypass-sensitive-data flags). No statement connects the OS-root requirement to, or distinguishes it from, any Server RBAC role a user might also need to authenticate to the cluster itself. This is the clearest instance in the batch of the round's authorship-provenance axis: a page an engineer would write exactly this way (root access is the only permission model that matters to the tool's own implementation) but a TW doing a security-conscious pass might add an RBAC cross-reference.

cross_component_finding: The tool's log table spans every Couchbase service (ns_server.analytics*.log, ns_server.eventing.log, ns_server.fts.log, ns_server.query.log, ns_server.goxdcr.log/ns_server.xdcr*.log, ns_server.indexer.log) plus the Backup Service (backup_service.log) and cbstats output (stats.log) - cbcollect_info is a single tool whose scope crosses all seven Couchbase services, unlike almost anything else in this batch which is scoped to one tool or one service.
